items.title: Factors Affecting the magnitude of Hydration Energy

source_refs.note: Factors Affecting the magnitude of Hydration Energy: a main subheading of 6.9.1 Hydration, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 131-131.

blocks.text: The heat of hydration depends on following factors:

We use a combined term for these two factors i.e., “charge density” defined as charge per unit area. If greater charge is present on smaller ion, the charge density is large and vice versa. And large value of charge density means that ions are strongly attracted by water molecules during the process of hydration, thereby increasing the hydration energy values. Bottom row: a small circle Mg2+, the sign greater than, a medium circle Ca2+, the sign greater than, a large circle Sr2+ (Mg2+ > Ca2+ > Sr2+).

blocks.text: On the same basis we can explain the hydration energy of anions.
